luke.7.p1.b1.text: When Jesus had concluded His discourse in the hearing of the people, He went to Capernaum.

luke.7.p1.b2.text: There a highly valued servant of a centurion was sick and about to die.

luke.7.p1.b3.text: … he sent some Jewish elders to ask Him to come and heal his servant.

luke.7.p1.b4.text: “This man is worthy to have You grant this, for he loves our nation and has built our synagogue.”

luke.7.p2.b1.text: So Jesus went with them. But when He was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends with the message:

luke.7.p2.b2.text: “Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy to have You come under my roof.

luke.7.p2.b3.text: That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to You. But just say the word, and my servant will be healed.

luke.7.p3.b1.text: “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”

luke.7.p3.b2.text: And when the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health.

luke.7.p4.b1.text: Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with Him, accompanied by a large crowd.

luke.7.p4.b2.text: the only son of his mother, and she was a widow.

luke.7.p4.b3.text: As He approached the town gate, He saw a dead man being carried out, … And a large crowd from the town was with her.

luke.7.p5.b1.text: When the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her

luke.7.p5.b4.text: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.

luke.7.p6.b1.text: “A great prophet has appeared among us!”

luke.7.p6.b3.text: And the news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and all the surrounding region.

luke.7.p7.b1.text: Then John’s disciples informed him about all these things.

luke.7.p7.b2.text: “Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?”

luke.7.p7.b3.text: “John the Baptist sent us to ask, ‘Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?’”

luke.7.p8.b1.text: At that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind.

luke.7.p8.b2.text: “Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard: … the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor.

luke.7.p8.b3.text: Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me.”

luke.7.p9.b1.text: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?

luke.7.p9.b2.text: Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces.

luke.7.p9.b3.text: What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

luke.7.p10.b1.text: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You.’

luke.7.p10.b2.text: I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John,

luke.7.p10.b3.text: yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”

luke.7.p11.b1.text: … even the tax collectors, … had received the baptism of John.

luke.7.p11.b2.text: All the people who heard this, … acknowledged God’s justice.

luke.7.p11.b3.text: But the Pharisees and experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.

luke.7.p12.b1.text: “To what, then, can I compare the men of this generation? What are they like?

luke.7.p12.b2.text: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another:

luke.7.p12.b3.text: ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance;

luke.7.p12.b4.text: we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’

luke.7.p13.b1.text: For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon!’

luke.7.p13.b2.text: The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

luke.7.p13.b3.text: But wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”

luke.7.p14.b1.text: Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him, and He entered the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.

luke.7.p14.b2.text: When a sinful woman from that town learned that Jesus was dining there, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.

luke.7.p14.b3.text: As she stood behind Him at His feet weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears and wipe them with her hair.

luke.7.p14.b4.text: Then she kissed His feet and anointed them with the perfume.

luke.7.p15.b1.text: “If this man were a prophet, He would know who this is and what kind of woman is touching Him—for she is a sinner!”

luke.7.p15.b2.text: “Simon, I have something to tell you.”

luke.7.p15.b3.text: “Two men were debtors to a certain moneylender. One owed him five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.

luke.7.p15.b4.text: “I suppose the one who was forgiven more,”

luke.7.p16.b1.text: And turning toward the woman, He said to Simon,

luke.7.p16.b3.text: When I entered your house, you did not give Me water for My feet, but she wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.

luke.7.p16.b4.text: You did not anoint My head with oil, but she has anointed My feet with perfume.

luke.7.p17.b1.text: Therefore I tell you, because her many sins have been forgiven, she has loved much.

luke.7.p17.b2.text: But he who has been forgiven little loves little.”

luke.7.p18.b1.text: “Who is this who even forgives sins?”

luke.7.p18.b2.text: “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”
